findings.title: canManage() grants manage-all-groups to admins who only have the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Any admin holding only an all-groups `view` permission therefore passes `canManage()`. This is a privilege escalation. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. `canManage(GroupModel)` and `canManageMembership` also depend on it. The check should only accept `MANAGE`. The interface Javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the mistake ("VIEW or MANAGE") and should be fixed too.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes up resource id, resource name and group id
findings.body: In V2 a group's resource is named with the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and `getOrCreateResource` uses it as the name). Here the lambda passes `groupResource.getId()` (the resource UUID) to `hasPermission`, which looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. That lookup misses, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource. The method then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result instead of the group id (resource name), so the returned set does not contain group ids. In addition, resources created by `getOrCreateResource` get no type, so `findByType(..., "Groups")` probably does not return per-group resources at all. Callers pass this set to `searchForUserStream` (via `UserModel.GROUPS`) and to `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. They will get wrong or empty group sets, so user counts and queries restricted by group permissions will be wrong. The tests miss this because `canView(user)` filters the result afterwards. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the result, and make sure per-group resources are actually found.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource is missing
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` can return null (schema not supported, or the resource was not created). The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. A null here gives an NPE and a 500 instead of a plain deny. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: V2 group permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on paths that are still reachable
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2` now overrides `groups()` for V2 and makes `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions` and similar methods throw. `GroupResource.getManagementPermissions` and `setManagementPermissionsEnabled` still call these when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. The `GroupRemovedEvent` listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calls `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. If the V1 feature is enabled alongside V2, those paths now fail with a 500 where before they worked, because `groups()` used to return the V1 implementation.

findings.title: Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and canManage() is inaccurate
findings.body: The Javadoc says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but the method returns a `Set<String>`. The `canManage()` Javadoc (lines 73-77) says V2 also grants it for VIEW permission on groups. That documents the bug in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` as intended behavior.

findings.title: No negative tests for view-only permission or group-id-based counting
findings.body: No test checks that an all-groups permission with only `VIEW` (or only a per-group `VIEW`) is denied for manage operations such as creating a group. That is the case that exposes the `canManage()` bug. Nothing exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` or the users count endpoint with group permissions. User search tests pass only because results are filtered again afterwards. Tests for those cases would have caught the wrong id and name usage.
